messages.author: 146a54acf88740fd
messages.subject: Spatotemporal dataset creation
parts:
Hi all.
after many years of using primarily Stan, I would like to revamp INLA.
So I would like to produce a dataset that has an auto-correlated spatiotemporal component (like the one presented in the book of  Blangiardo e Cameletti, 2015: Spatial and Spatiotemporal models with R inla). 
But rather than starting for real measures I would like to set the parameters of the model and simulate the spatiotemporal model.
Is there a resource online to help me starting this work, maybe using the RandomFields package too?

Thanks in advance!

messages.author: 66ed4f72a898a51c
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Spatotemporal dataset creation
parts:
Hi Fabio,

I am not sure if you want to sample from spatio-temporal models in the
discrete or in the continuous domain, even though the RandomFields
package is for the continuous domain case.

In the discrete domain case, the inla.knmodels.sample() can be used to
sample from the (scaled) separable (covariance/precision)
spatio-temporal models introduced in
https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/10960871/
and you can also easily build a variety of separable spatio temporal
models considering other spatial and temporal models in a similar
fashion building the precision matrix and then using the
inla.qsample() function.

In the continuous domain case, the new INLAspacetime package could be
considered for some of the separable and nonseparable spatio-temporal
models presented in https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.04917

best regards,
Elias

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Spatotemporal dataset creation

using the randomfields package is ok for simulating data. the books at
r-inla.org (available on www) would be useful, especially the SPDE book.

note that the INLAspacetime R-package contains the new non-separable
space-time models develloped, see the arxiv preprint for details

Best
H
